LanguageData.Stagecraft_SetPlaceTip: Adds a "Location" line to the environment part of every RimTalk prompt: your own colony, another faction's settlement (and whether they are hostile), a quest site (and for which quest), a cave or other map inside a map (and where it is entered from), and the region and landmark on the world map. Shown only while RimTalk's weather context is on. To write this line yourself, select a place on the world map and press "Location description", or use the button below while in a game.
LanguageData.Stagecraft_SetTargets: Say who the people a job is aimed at are
LanguageData.Stagecraft_SetTargetsTip: "Tending to Mira" or "Delivering food to Bob" gives only a name, and when that pawn is not nearby the model has to guess who it is. With this on, the name is followed by what they are to the colony: (colonist), (prisoner), (guest), (animal, dog), (mechanoid) and so on. When RimTalk's context optimization is off, RimTalk writes this itself at more length and nothing is added here.
LanguageData.Stagecraft_SetConditions: Bring up lasting conditions again while they last
LanguageData.Stagecraft_SetConditionsTip: RimTalk gives a letter one chance to be talked about, in the two hours after it arrives, and then forgets it. A cold snap, an eclipse or toxic fallout that lasts for days is brought up a few more times while it lasts, and the letter's own chance is made up for if nobody took it. Only when someone is awake and there are no enemies on the map.
LanguageData.Stagecraft_SetConditionTalks: At most {0} talks per condition (the letter's included, about one every day and a half)
LanguageData.Stagecraft_SetConditionSkip: Conditions never to bring up again:
LanguageData.Stagecraft_SetConditionSkipTip: Their def names (such as ColdSnap, Aurora), separated by commas or spaces.
LanguageData.Stagecraft_SetConditionLines: List current conditions in the environment
LanguageData.Stagecraft_SetConditionLinesTip: Lists the conditions in the environment part of every prompt. Pawns then mention them in passing very often (one condition came up seven times in two and a half days in testing), so this is off by default.
LanguageData.Stagecraft_SetQuestTalk: Talk a quest over as soon as it is accepted
LanguageData.Stagecraft_SetQuestTalkTip: When you accept a quest, an awake colonist is found at once to talk over the plan, who goes and what to bring. If nobody can take it, it keeps trying for half a day.
LanguageData.Stagecraft_SetNotesTip: In RimTalk's "talk to" window, text between two pairs of slashes is not said aloud by anyone: the model writes the whole conversation it describes, with the chosen pawn speaking first, for example //Amy and Bob argue about dinner, Bob gives in//. Turned off, such text is spoken as a line, the way RimTalk does it.
LanguageData.Stagecraft_SetSpeakTip: Guests, traders and prisoners, who you cannot give orders to, get a button: pick someone for them to talk to, then let the AI write it or write their line or a director's note yourself. They must first be allowed to talk in RimTalk's settings.
LanguageData.Stagecraft_SetLiteratureTip: When RimTalk Literature has the AI write books, journals or art descriptions, this text is added to the end of its prompts. Its prompts say nothing about the setting, and in a medieval game it wrote a diary full of patrol robots and satellite stations. A few lines about your game's era, what exists and what does not, are enough; left empty, nothing is added. Of no use without RimTalk Literature.
